channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest
channel.description: This week's upcoming Gov-Hub meetings and community events across the Telluride region (Town of Telluride, Mountain Village, San Miguel County, the Sheridan Opera House, The Alibi, Wilkinson Library, KOTO, telluride.com, and more).

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Oct 30–5
item.description: The biggest thing on the docket this week is a Telluride Medical Center special meeting where the board takes up a proposal to engage Jensen Partners for due diligence with CommonSpirit Health — one of the country's largest hospital systems — a signal that a formal partnership or affiliation could be moving forward. Alongside that, Ouray City Council holds a public hearing on its 2027 budget and votes on second reading of two ordinances setting utility rates and adding a new light-industrial rate category, while Telluride's Ecology Commission takes up a draft ordinance that would ban gas-powered lawn equipment in town limits by 2028–2030. Halloween weekend kicks things off with the parade, Young Frankenstein at the high school, and a full slate of community events before the week turns to Mountainfilm for Locals.

item.title: [Sat, Oct 31] YOUNG FRANKENSTEIN – THE MUSICAL (a TMHS & Telluride Theatre Co-Production)
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Michael D. Palm Theater, Telluride It's okay to LAUGH during spooky season… we invite you to join us for Mel Brooks' classic comedy: YOUNG FRANKENSTEIN – THE MUSICAL! Based on the film starring Gene Wilder, this musical pokes fun at Mary Shelly's "Frankenstein," along with other classic monster movies. This production is performed and designed by our very own students at Telluride Middle-High School, under the mentorship of Telluride Theatre and the R-1 School District. Grandson of the infamous Victor Frankenstein, Frederick Frankenstein (pronounced "Fronk-en-steen") inherits his family's estate in Transylvania. With the help of a hunchbacked sidekick, Igor, and a yodeling lab assistant, Inga, Frederick finds himself in the mad scientist shoes of his ancestors. "It's alive!" he exclaims as he brings to life a creature to rival his grandfather's. Eventually, of course, the monster escapes, and hilarity ensues. Have a laugh this Halloween & support our local students. Costumes encouraged! …

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Ouray City Council Regular Meeting — 2026-11-02
item.description:
ouraycity • 2026-11-02
The main business this evening is the 2027 budget. Council holds a public hearing on the proposed City of Ouray budget and takes up two ordinances on second reading: Ordinance 7 sets the 2027 rates for water, sewer, surcharge, refuse, and recycling; Ordinance 8 amends the municipal code to add a rate category specifically for light industrial operations — a new wrinkle in how the city classifies utility customers. Council also considers ratifying a Caterpillar equipment lease-purchase agreement and approving an MOU with the Ridgway Fire Protection District covering fire, EMS, training, and operational cooperation. On the liquor license side, The Yankee Girl Café has a new application before the council. The consent agenda includes four appointments to the Main Street Committee and a liquor license renewal for Ouray Lodge No. 492.
⚡ Why it matters: Public hearing on Ouray's 2027 budget; second-reading votes on utility and industrial rate ordinances.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Ecology Commission - Nov 04 2026 — 2026-11-04
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-11-04
The Ecology Commission meets to finalize its 2027 workplan and, more consequentially, to discuss a draft ordinance that would phase out combustion-powered lawn and garden equipment within town limits. The proposed ordinance — a new Article 10 added to Chapter 7 of the Municipal Code — would ban gas-powered leaf blowers by 2028 and all other covered equipment by 2030. The recitals cite the box canyon's particular sensitivity to noise (90–110 decibels, amplified by the terrain) and air quality impacts. Colorado's HB23-1161 already provides a 30% point-of-sale discount on electric replacements, and the San Miguel Power Association offers additional rebates up to 25%, potentially offsetting roughly half the replacement cost. Exceptions are included for pre-adoption dual-use enclosed-cab tractors. The commission also votes to formally adopt its 2027 workplan, which carries forward ongoing threads: the Climate Action Plan update, bear safety programming, Trash Bash, Green Grants, and landscaping ordinance advocacy.
⚡ Why it matters: Draft ordinance would ban gas-powered lawn equipment in Telluride by 2028���2030.

item.description:

The more consequential work happens in the afternoon worksession: the Grant Subcommittee's financial training, a discussion of 2027 grant guidelines and philosophies, and a first look at revised 2027 special event policies. The subcommittee also brings back a recommendation on grant application discrepancies it flagged at its October 23 meeting.
